name: Crossplane
summary: A Kubernetes-native control plane framework that composes custom APIs into managed resources, runs composition functions, and reconciles external services through provider controllers.

features.name: Function-pipeline composition
features.description: A Composition selects a composite resource type and invokes an ordered pipeline of functions to build desired composed resources from observed state.
benefits: Provides reusable API-to-resource composition and extension points
costs: Pipeline ordering, desired-state copying, and function availability constrain behavior

features.name: Provider-managed external resource boundary
features.description: Providers install Kubernetes APIs for external resources and run controllers that observe managed resources and create or update corresponding resources in an external system.
benefits: Separates external API integration from core composition logic
costs: Provider versions, credentials, and external API semantics affect reconciliation

features.name: Desired-versus-observed reconciliation
features.description: Crossplane compares managed-resource intent with external observations and repeatedly reconciles creation, update, deletion, status, and connection details.
benefits: Supports declarative convergence and drift correction
costs: External side effects, retries, and finalizers make convergence asynchronous

mathematical_views.question: How does a composite resource and its observed composed resources produce a desired resource set?
assumptions: Functions are ordered stages with request and response state
Each stage preserves desired state it does not intentionally remove
The view does not claim atomicity across composed resources

mathematical_views.question: Under what observations and permissions does a managed resource converge toward an external resource specification?
assumptions: The Kubernetes managed resource is the source of truth for forProvider fields
Provider observations may be delayed or fail
Finalizers model deletion until the external resource is gone

mathematical_views.question: How do provider packages, revisions, runtime pods, APIs, and managed-resource controllers depend on one another?
assumptions: Package installation creates API and runtime/controller nodes
A provider controller watches the managed-resource kinds it supports
The graph abstracts package registry availability and image execution

benefits: Reusable infrastructure APIs with programmable composition
costs: Pipeline contracts and missing desired-state fields can alter or delete composed resources

benefits: Broad external-system integration without embedding every API in core
costs: Credential, provider-version, and API compatibility become operational dependencies
Eventual convergence and external side effects require retries, finalizers, and observability
